note: The snowflake MCP server answers in a YAML-ish block with a random `data_id`, where `sql` returns JSON, so the MCP side of each case is projected with `pipe`. Every snowflake projection ends in `grep .`, so an arm whose reply carries no such line fails the case instead of agreeing on nothing.

cases.name: read_query
cases.why: the same statement returns the same rows through either arm

args.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS N FROM LANDING_TASK_REMINDER.PUBLIC.EMPLOYEE

mirage.command: snowflake read-query '{"query":"SELECT COUNT(*) AS N FROM LANDING_TASK_REMINDER.PUBLIC.EMPLOYEE"}'

cases.name: read_query_rows
cases.why: a multi-row read agrees value for value, not just in count

args.query: SELECT NAME FROM LANDING_TASK_REMINDER.PUBLIC.EMPLOYEE ORDER BY NAME LIMIT 5

mirage.command: snowflake read-query '{"query":"SELECT NAME FROM LANDING_TASK_REMINDER.PUBLIC.EMPLOYEE ORDER BY NAME LIMIT 5"}'
